facts.text: Coeymans takes its name from Dutch settler Barent Pieterse Koeymans, who arrived in 1639 and secured a land patent in 1673.
In the early 20th century, the Powell & Minnock Brick Company, founded in 1895, became the leading brick producer north of Coeymans.
The Ariantje Coeymans House, built around 1720, stands as one of the Hudson Valley’s oldest surviving Dutch colonial structures.
Shipbuilding surged at Coeymans Landing after the War of 1812, keeping the riverport busy until the early 1900s.
A brief railroad link to Albany opened in 1864, later expanded by the New York West Shore Railroad in 1883 to serve Coeymans Junction.
Today, the Port of Coeymans and the Lafarge Cement Plant drive the town’s economy, built on the former Powell & Minnock brick site.
